extracted.intended_audience: Korean Intellectual Property Office examiners; patent applicants and patent attorneys (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for examination and processing of applications to register patent term extensions (by regulatory approval and by delay in registration) under the Korean Patent Act, including eligibility, required evidence, amendment rules, notices, calculation of extension periods, and what counts as applicant-caused delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner determination of necessity of approval
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner generally need not examine whether approval under relevant provisions to manufacture the drug is necessary, unless special conditions (e.g., third-party objection) exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner is unsure of the necessity of approval, he/she may conduct an additional examination (request opinion from relevant organizations, etc.). If the results show approval is not required, the examiner shall notify the ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identicalness of composition between patented substance and approved substance
rubrics_metrics.description: For an invention subject to patent term extension by approval, the approved substance must have the same composition as the substance recited in the claims (for substance inventions) or as the matter manufactured by the claimed method (for method inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compositions are not identical, the examiner shall deem it a ground for rejection under Article 91(1). (i) Where the claimed subject matter is a substance invention, compare the claimed substance and the approved substance. (ii) Where the claimed subject matter is a manufacturing-method invention, compare the substance manufactured by the disclosed method with the approved substance; manufacturing methods themselves need not be compared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identicalness of use between patented use invention and approved substance
rubrics_metrics.description: When the patented subject matter is a use invention, the use of the approved substance must be the same as the use disclosed in the patent; otherwise the patent term shall not be extended even if compositions are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patented use includes use of the approved substance, it shall be deemed that the uses are the same (i.e., extension may be allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility of intermediates, catalysts, and manufacturing devices for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights covering manufacturing devices for a final product, catalysts used in manufacturing an intermediate or final product, or intermediates themselves are not subject to patent term extension based on approval of a final product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts governing safety (e.g., Pharmaceutical Affairs Act) apply to final products, not intermediates. If an extension application for an intermediate, catalyst, or manufacturing device is filed on the basis of approval of a final product, the examiner shall notify the ground for rejection under Article 91(1)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must have obtained regulatory approval (patentee/licensee registration rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval necessary for term extension must have been obtained by the patentee or a person who has an exclusive or non-exclusive license under the patent right, subject to registration rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only some of multiple patentees or licensees have obtained a license it is deemed that approval has been obtained. However, if a patentee or licensee who was not registered at the time of filing the extension application obtained approval, it shall be deemed a ground for rejection under Article 91(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum extension period and its calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The extension applied for must not exceed the period during which the patented invention could not have been practiced; calculation of the term for which extension is applied shall be conducted based on calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applied-for extension need not exactly match the actual unpracticed period. If the term applied for has not elapsed even if incorrectly calculated, the examiner shall acknowledge the term rather than notify rejection. Note: if approval date is before the date of registration establishing the patent right, that situation falls under grounds for rejection (Article 91(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility for registration of extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant who files for registration of a patent term extension must be the patentee at the time of filing; a licensee (exclusive or non-exclusive) cannot be the applicant for registration of extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where irregularities exist (e.g., an ineligible person filed), the examiner shall notify grounds for rejection rather than issuing an amendment request or returning the application. For jointly owned patent rights, the extension application must be filed by all co-owners; filing by only some co-owners is a ground for rejection (Article 91(1)(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of ground for rejection: content and argument period
rubrics_metrics.description: When intending to reject an extension application under the applicable provisions, the examiner shall notify the applicant of the ground for rejection and give an opportunity to submit written arguments within a designated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must indicate relevant provisions or grounds precisely and concisely so the applicant clearly understands them. The examiner shall notify that written argument must be submitted within two months. The period can be extended up to one additional month each time, up to three times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of written arguments and timing/eligibility of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: After a notice of ground for rejection, an applicant may submit written arguments or amendments; the examiner must consider submitted arguments and re-examine amended matters when amendments are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written argument shall be submitted within the designated period; even if submitted late (after period) or before notice, the examiner shall take the argument into consideration rather than returning it. An amendment can be presented before delivery of a copy of the decision to grant registration of extension, but after notice of grounds for rejection amendments are only allowed within the argument period. Matters eligible for amendment under Article 90(6) include: (①) indication of claims for registration of extension, ② the period for extension request, ③ the content of approval/registration under Article 89, ④ the ground for extension specified in Ordinance of the Ministry). Amendments are severely restricted: clerical-error-type corrections may be allowed; amendments to add co-owners, change applicant where not legitimate, or amend after termination of proceedings are not acknowledged. If an amendment is not legitimate, examiner shall deliver a preliminary notice for inadmissible amendment and proceed accordingly. When an amendment is recognized legitimate, the amended application is examined as if submitted at the initial filing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on certain corrections and inadmissible amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain corrections (e.g., changing applicant name to a patentee who was not the patentee at time of filing, adding co-owners to cure defective filing, or changing patent number generally) are not acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing an applicant to a universal successor in presence of universal succession is not acknowledged. Article 90(6) allows changes of contents claimed at filing, but changing a patent number is generally not allowed except for correction of a clerical error where patent number, application number, application date, patent date, title, etc. are considered together. If amendment is not eligible, the examiner issues a preliminary notice for inadmissible amendment; failure to correct leads to examination of the pre-amendment application and possible refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to register or reject: required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A written decision to register an extension or to reject an application must be prepared and signed by the examiner and reported to the team leader, and must include specified items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items: ① Number of application for registration of extension; ② Patent number; ③ Period for extension; ④ Content of approval/registration under Article 89 (claims for registration, content of approval/registration, ground for extension, etc.); ⑤ Name and address of applicant (or title/address of legal entity); ⑥ Agent name/address or firm/title for an agent; ⑦ Order of decision and ground for the decision; ⑧ Date of decision. Items ③ and ④ need not be written in a written decision to reject the registration application of extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal and publication following registration of extension
rubrics_metrics.description: When a decision to register an extension is made, the Commissioner shall deliver a copy to the applicant and the registration division shall include specified items for registration in the patent gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent gazette items to include: ① name and address of patent right holder (or title/business address for legal entity), ② patent number, ③ date of registration of extension, ④ period for extension, ⑤ content of approval under Article 89 (indications such as claims for registration of extension, contents of approval/registration, ground for extension, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and invalidation rights and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural remedies available after a decision to reject registration of extension include an appeal trial and an invalidation trial under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person who received a written decision to reject registration of extension may submit a notice of appeal within thirty days from the date of receipt of the copy of the decision. If the registration falls under Article 134(1), an applicant can request a trial to invalidate the registration of patent term extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of patent term for delays in registration (Article 92-2 eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: When registration of a patent right is delayed beyond specified time thresholds, the patent term may be extended by the delayed period (subject to reductions for applicant-caused delay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registration is delayed more than four years from the filing date of the patent application or three years from the date a request for examination is made, whichever is later, the term of the relevant patent may be extended by the delayed period (notwithstanding Article 88(1)). Periods delayed due to the applicant shall be reduced from the extension; if applicant-caused delay overlaps with the registration delay, reduction shall not exceed the actual applicant-caused delay. Matters concerning what constitutes 'period delayed due to an applicant' are prescribed by Presidential Decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates to be deemed filing date for computing the four-year threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating the four-year period from filing date under Article 92-2, certain alternative dates are deemed the filing date in specific situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates deemed as filing date include: 1) date a legitimate right-holder applies where application is by legitimate right-holder under Articles 34/35; 2) date a divisional application is filed (Article 52); 3) date a converted application is filed (Article 53); 4) date a document containing matters of Article 203(1) is submitted for an international application deemed a patent application (Article 199(1)); 5) date an applicant requests KIPO decision under Article 214(1) for an international application deemed a patent application (Article 214); 6) the patent application filing date in other cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'period delayed due to an applicant' (Enforcement Decree Article 7(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The period delayed due to an applicant' for purposes of Article 92-2 is expressly defined to include many specific patent-proceeding, litigation, and administrative-appeal periods when delay is attributable to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included periods (selected list as enumerated): (1) In patent-related proceedings pending before KIPO or the Trial & Appeal Board: (a) period from ordering appointment/replacement of an agent to appointment, (b) extended periods at applicant's request, (c) postponed dates for patent-related proceedings at applicant's request, (d) period from cessation of a cause not attributable to applicant to completion, (e) suspension/interruptions under Articles 20/23(2)/78(1)/164(1), (f) periods to report consultation results under Article 36(6), (g) period until specification amended as required under Article 42(5), (h) periods ordered for amendment under Articles 46/141(1)/203(2), (i) period from making to withdrawing a priority claim under Article 56, (j) delayed determination of expedited examination under Article 10, (k) period while applicant responds to grounds for rejection under Article 63(1) (with exceptions), (l) periods related to payment/exemption of patent fees after receipt of certified copy of decision to grant, (m) period from service of certified copy of decision to reject to request for reexamination, (n) period when request for examination/reexamination is made after cause not attributable to applicant ceases under Article 67-3(1), (o) suspension period where motions for disqualification/recusal are unresolved under Articles 149/150/152/153, (p) period for examination/preservation of evidence requested by applicants under Article 157 when such process concludes it is unnecessary, (q) periods when review on merits is resumed after closing upon applicants' request, (r) period from awareness of grounds for retrial to filing retrial, (s) periods when presiding judge grants additional period under Article 186(5), (t) periods of delayed service of documents or service by publication due to applicant. (2) In litigation concerning trial decisions or court decisions: specified stay/suspension periods, delays due to motions for disqualification/recusal, court-ordered corrections, appointment of special representatives, resumed trials due to applicant, hearing postponements caused by applicant, extensions/grants of additional periods at applicant request, and other service delays attributable to applicant. (3) In administrative appeal or litigation on administrative dispositions: analogous periods where delay is attributable to the appellant/applicant, including Commission-ordered corrections, deadlines for supplemental briefs, postponed hearing dates at applicant request, and service delays.  (The enforcement decree lists many subitems in detail; examiners should apply the full enumerated list when determining applicant-caused delay reductions.)
